Bargur.origin_region: Bargur forest hills, Anthiyur taluk, Erode district, Tamil Nadu
Bargur.milk_yield: 250 - 600 kg per lactation (predominantly rugged draught breed)
Bargur.characteristics: Medium-sized, fiery and alert temperament, brown coat with distinctive white patches and speckles, extraordinary endurance in rocky hill terrain.
Bargur.identification_features: Brown coat with white speckles/splashes, light muzzle, medium horns sweeping backwards and outwards with sharp tips, compact nimble frame.

Hallikar.origin_region: Hallikar belt (Mysuru, Mandya, Hassan, Tumakuru), Karnataka
Hallikar.milk_yield: 500 - 1,100 kg per lactation (premier South Indian draught breed)
Hallikar.characteristics: Medium to large build, grey to dark grey coat, renowned trotting speed and hardiness, historical foundation breed for Amrit Mahal draught cattle.
Hallikar.identification_features: Long, vertically rising tapering horns turning backward with sharp pointed tips, prominent bulging forehead, deep compact chest.

Gir.origin_region: Gir hills and forests of South Kathiawar, Gujarat
Gir.characteristics: Distinctive convex forehead acting as a shield for brain, long pendulous ears folded like a palm leaf, reddish-brown to speckled white coat.
Gir.identification_features: Prominent rounded forehead, drooping ears, dark pigmentation around eyes, half-moon curved horns turning backwards.

Sahiwal.origin_region: Montgomery district (now Sahiwal in Punjab, Pakistan / Punjab India border)
Sahiwal.characteristics: Heavy body, reddish brown skin, loose skin skin folds (hence 'Zebu'), high heat tolerance and tick resistance.
Sahiwal.identification_features: Reddish brown to pale red color, voluminous dewlap, short stumpy horns, large naval flap in females.

Red_Sindhi.origin_region: Sindh province (historically bred in organized farms across India)
Red_Sindhi.characteristics: Deep red to yellowish red body, compact and symmetrical frame, highly resistant to tropical diseases.
Red_Sindhi.identification_features: Dark red color, heavy head with thick thick curved horns, prominent hump in males.

Kankrej.origin_region: Rann of Kutch, Gujarat and adjoining Barmer/Jalore districts of Rajasthan
Kankrej.characteristics: Dual-purpose breed famous for 'Sawai Chaal' (characteristic majestic gait). Silver-grey to iron-grey coloration.
Kankrej.identification_features: Large lyre-shaped horns covered with skin at base, broad dished forehead, strong neck.

Tharparkar.origin_region: Thar Desert, Sindh / Rajasthan border (Jodhpur, Jaisalmer)
Tharparkar.characteristics: Dual purpose, renowned desert adaptability, coat color changes from white in winter to greyish in summer.
Tharparkar.identification_features: Lyre-shaped medium horns, white or light grey coat, black hooves and muzzle, medium pendulous ears.

Ongole.origin_region: Prakasam and Guntur districts, Andhra Pradesh
Ongole.characteristics: Heavy draft and milk breed, famous globally (exported to Brazil as Nellore). Glossy white/grey coat.
Ongole.identification_features: Large muscular frame, prominent hump, dark markings around eyes and neck, stumpy horns.

Murrah.origin_region: Rohtak, Hisar, and Jind districts of Haryana; Delhi NCR
Murrah.characteristics: Premier dairy buffalo breed of the world ('Black Gold' of India). Deep jet-black skin.
Murrah.identification_features: Tightly curled ring-like horns, jet black color, white switch of tail (optional), wedge-shaped body.

Jaffarabadi.origin_region: Gir forest, Gir Somnath, and Amreli districts of Gujarat
Jaffarabadi.characteristics: Massive heavy buffalo breed, broad head, highly prized for butterfat content in milk.
Jaffarabadi.identification_features: Heavy drooping horns covering side of face and neck, prominent bulging forehead, deep massive torso.

Surti.origin_region: Kaira, Vadodara, and Surat districts of Gujarat
Surti.characteristics: Medium-sized docile buffalo, rusty brown to black skin, highly efficient coarse fodder converter.
Surti.identification_features: Flat sickle-shaped horns, two white collars on brisket ('V-shaped' chevron white marks), dark skin.

Mehsana.origin_region: Mehsana, Banaskantha, and Sabarkantha districts of Gujarat
Mehsana.characteristics: Crossbreed derivative of Murrah and Surti, high milk consistency and long lactation length.
Mehsana.identification_features: Slightly curled horns (less tightly curled than Murrah, longer than Surti), black to brown skin, medium ears.

Nili_Ravi.origin_region: Sutlej and Ravi river belts of Punjab
Nili_Ravi.characteristics: Distinctive wall eyes, high milk producer, prefers river/water wallowing habitats.
Nili_Ravi.identification_features: White markings on forehead ('Panj Kalyan'), muzzle, legs, and tail switch; pinkish markings on udder; wall (blue/white) eyes.
